description:
FILED s484a (Opus, 2026-09-13), the measured residue of #1587.  s484a made the
eval collapse accept `package NAME VERSION` and `package NAME BLOCK` in every
spelling INCLUDING the flattened bare-block one, which carried uni/opcroak.t
from an aborted eval to a running file -- but op/inccode-tie.t did NOT move
(0/0, the same refusal), and this is why.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 accepts it, `$@` empty; PCL refuses):

    eval '{ my $al; package AI { sub AUTOLOAD { $al = 1 } sub DESTROY {} }
            push @main::z, 1;
            my $e = 1; }';
    print "err=[$@]\n";

    perl: err=[]
    PCL : err=[PCL: unsupported in string eval: multiple package sections]

THE SHAPE.  A BARE BLOCK containing a BLOCK-FORM package, whose statements
AFTER the package block are not literal-only.  op/inccode.t line 182 is
exactly that, and op/inccode-tie.t is a four-line wrapper that `do`s it, so
the whole 89-row file sits behind this one eval:

    {
        my $autoloaded;
        package AutoInc {
            sub AUTOLOAD { ... }
            sub DESTROY {}
        }
        push @INC, bless {}, "AutoInc";      # <-- the non-literal tail
        $evalret = eval { require Quux3; 1 };
        ...
    }

WHY IT IS STILL REFUSED, and it is a DELIBERATE stop, not an oversight: the
T-A1 flattening ERASES the bare block, so both the leading and the trailing
statements lose their block scope.  s353's two whitelists are what license the
collapse -- `_eval_safe_leading_stmts` for the head and
`_eval_literal_only_stmts` for the tail -- and s484a kept the tail rule for
exactly the flattened case (`$erased`, keyed on the blockform segment's `blk`
tag).  A `push @INC, ...` tail is not literal-only, so the arm declines and
the ruled refusal fires.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT (not designed): the tail rule is conservative for the BLOCK
form in a way it is not for the statement form.  s353's stated reason for
literal-only is that "a trailing expression with a name in it would resolve in
the region package X where perl, back outside the block, resolves it in the
CALLER's package" -- and for a BLOCK form that reason does not apply at all:
`_lower_block`'s `if ($blk)` arm emits a RESTORE after the block, so the tail
already resolves in the outer package by construction (probed in s484a:
`eval 'package Foo { our $x = 1 } our $x = 7; $x'` is 7 with `$Foo::x` 1).
What remains is only the erased LEXICAL scope of the bare block, which matters
for a `my` declared in it -- and in a one-shot eval the lifetime is the same.
So the candidate is: for a blockform whose `blk` is set, replace the
literal-only tail rule with the same M1 whitelist the HEAD uses (or with
"no `my` whose scope is observable after the eval"), and measure.

BAR: op/inccode-tie.t 0/0 -> its 89 rows (the file's own snapshot says
`P: 89/0`), uni/opcroak.t unchanged, the seven-spelling table in
scratch/s484a/probes/p1587.pl and the six-shape table in
scratch/s484a/probes/f1587.pl both unmoved, guard rows beside the #1587 block
in Pl/t/parser2-02.t (which currently asserts this refusal -- the s416
stale-guard rule: REWRITE that row in the same commit), corpus-diff +
emission-ab + the gate-set scan over both populations (a refusal that stops
firing is a checker narrowing, the s372 rule), and the full sweep.
SIZE: S-M.
